title: Rav Tuvi bar Rav Mattenah
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He had a brother named Rav Achdevoi, and also a sister, as related in Bava Batra 151a: his sister wrote her property over to Rav Tuvi in the morning. His brother Rav Achdevoi came to her weeping and said to her, “Now they will say that my brother is a Torah scholar and I am not.” She wrote her property over to Rav Achdevoi in the evening, and Rav Nachman ruled that the latter acquired it.

In Rav Yosef’s days he was already a leading sage of the generation, as in Bava Batra 23a, where Rav Yosef said to Abaye: “Thus said Rav Tuvi bar Mattenah.” In Bava Kamma 36b: a man struck his fellow; Rav Tuviah (Dikdukei Soferim: Rav Tuvi) bar Mattenah sent before Rav Yosef: “Did we learn a Tyrian sela or a provincial sela?” He said to him: “You learned it” … he said to him: “Shall the Tanna go on reciting like a peddler?” In Chullin 39b: “Rav Tuvi bar Mattenah sent before Rav Yosef: In such a case, what? He sent to him: Thus said Rav Yehudah that Shmuel said.”

Hyman infers from this that he was a judge in his town near Pumbedita, Rav Yosef’s place. He also finds support in Moed Katan 16a: a certain butcher who behaved insolently toward Rav Tuvi bar Mattenah — Abaye and Rava took a vote concerning him and excommunicated him.
He is mentioned in Rosh Hashanah 19a regarding whether Megillat Taanit was annulled.

Hyman also locates his burial place in Abaye’s place, in Pumbedita, as related in Bava Batra 58a: a certain magus who used to dig up the dead — when he reached the cave of Rav Tuvi bar Mattenah, Rav Tuvi seized the grave robber by his beard. Abaye came and said to him, “Please let him go.” The next year he seized him again; Abaye came and asked him, and he did not let him go until they had to cut off the beard.

notes.text: Saved Davidson BavaKamma36b has רוכלא, peddler, versus supplied דוכלא; MoedKatan16a has דאיתפקר, behaved insolently, versus supplied דאיתפקד. These connected readings are disclosed rather than asserted as printed-pixel corrections. אימנו is took a vote, not were counted over him. In the grave narrative Tuvi seizes the intruder’s beard; the geographic and judicial inferences remain Hyman’s.

The consulted Bava Kamma 36b has the peddler expression and Moed Katan 16a has insolent conduct and a vote. The current corrections remain intact, including the sister’s morning/evening transfers and Tuvi seizing the grave robber’s beard. Hyman’s leading-generation, judicial and geographical conclusions are preserved as his inferences, not new site or identity bindings.
